stem: Which bundle of practices is supported by CDC guidance for reducing central line-associated bloodstream infection risk?

options.A: Use maximal sterile barriers for insertion, appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene and site care, and promptly remove the catheter when it is no longer essential.
options.B: Replace all central lines routinely every 24 hours regardless of indication, site condition, or ongoing clinical need.
options.C: Apply topical antibiotic ointment routinely to every central-line insertion site and omit sterile barriers during insertion.
options.D: Keep unnecessary central venous catheters in place until discharge because repeated insertion is always riskier than prolonged dwell time.

rationale: CDC central-line guidance recommends maximal sterile barrier precautions for CVC/PICC insertion, skin preparation with greater than 0.5% chlorhexidine in alcohol when not contraindicated, hand hygiene and aseptic catheter care, and prompt removal of intravascular catheters that are no longer essential. Routine replacement of CVCs to prevent infection is not recommended. A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply CDC-supported central-line infection-prevention practices: aseptic technique, maximal sterile barriers, appropriate chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, and prompt removal when the line is no longer essential.

source_claim_supported: CDC supports maximal sterile barriers, chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, hand hygiene/aseptic care, and prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters as infection-prevention measures.

source_original.stem: Which bundle of practices is supported by CDC guidance for reducing central line-associated bloodstream infection risk?

options.A: Use maximal sterile barriers, chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene, and remove the catheter promptly when no longer essential
options.B: Replace all central lines every 24 hours regardless of indication, site condition, or ongoing clinical need
options.C: Apply topical antibiotic ointment routinely to every central-line site and omit sterile barriers during insertion
options.D: Keep unnecessary central venous catheters in place until discharge because repeated insertion is always riskier

source_original.rationale: CDC's intravascular-catheter prevention recommendations support hand hygiene, maximal sterile barrier precautions for central-line insertion, chlorhexidine-based skin preparation when appropriate, and prompt removal of catheters that are no longer essential. Routine replacement without clinical indication is not recommended.
source_original.source_detail: Summary recommendations: hand hygiene; maximal sterile barrier precautions; >0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol for central-line skin preparation when appropriate; promptly remove intravascular catheters when no longer essential.

correction_summary: Retained key A, tightened the bundle to the exact CDC recommendations and explicitly contrasted it with the no-routine-replacement recommendation. Reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC primary infection-control guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC summary page dated 2024-02-28 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC maximal sterile barrier, skin preparation, catheter removal and replacement recommendations
audit_findings.claim_audit: Every keyed intervention is explicitly present in CDC guidance and no unsupported bundle component remains.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because routine scheduled CVC replacement is not recommended.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because omission of sterile barriers contradicts CDC insertion guidance and routine ointment is not the universal strategy proposed.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because CDC recommends prompt removal when a catheter is no longer essential.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A is a valid multicomponent CDC-supported prevention approach.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are central-line management bundles; the key is determined by infection-control evidence.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device infection prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the CDC central-line recommendations, all alternatives, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
